video_title: Kuminga BIG Help To Timberwolves? + SHOCKING NBA Awards Predictions

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's move to the Minnesota Timberwolves
quotes.excerpt: The Wolves are in real need of a starter power forward. Kuminga is in need of a team.
quotes.quote: The Wolves are in real need of a starter power forward. Kuminga is in need of a team where he has a big role that he can go back to the market next year and try to get the contract that he's wanted. He has wanted a starting role for a long time, and that's what he's getting here from day one, and they needed it. He's actually going to get more money than I thought he would get when he signed with the Wolves. The Wolves are going to have to create a roster spot.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Minnesota Timberwolves likely to move Josh Green
quotes.excerpt: They're going to have to figure out a way probably to dump Josh Green.
quotes.quote: They're going to have to figure out a way probably to dump Josh Green to be able to get to the taxpayer mid-level and stay under the second apron.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Cavaliers' interest in Cam Whitmore
quotes.excerpt: The Cavs recently traded for Cam Whitmore, and he's likely to be waived and stretched by Saturday.
quotes.quote: The Cavs recently traded for Cam Whitmore, and he's likely to be waived and stretched by Saturday. If you don't waive a player by Saturday, his contract can't be stretched. So, for example, the Cavs recently traded for Cam Whitmore, and he's likely to be waived and stretched by Saturday. That's why James Harden hasn't signed his contract yet, as an example. But anyway, that's neither here nor there. The Wolves are going to take a little bit of a bite on Josh Green, who, you know, is a rotation edge rotation player.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Jonathan Kuminga's decision to turn down the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: He turned down a three-year deal from the Lakers according to Shams.
quotes.quote: He turned down a three-year deal from the Lakers according to Shams. It would have paid about 12 per, and apparently the Lakers were recruiting him to be their starting power forward. Now, what he's saying is, I would rather have one year at six-ish than three at 36, because he thinks he's going to make clearly more than mid-level money coming off of this deal.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: The Pelicans are only about three million below the tax, and signing him to this would put them into the tax, which they don't want to do. So there's going to be a corresponding move that you're going to see beforehand.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim MacMahon
text_blocks.text: The Clippers have come to terms that they're not going to match anything and they're going to let Mathurin go. There may be a trade that ends up happening, but we'll see what goes on there. Again, I don't think they can sign and trade him.

quotes.summary_phrase: Pelicans' financial constraints regarding Benedict Mathurin
quotes.excerpt: The Pelicans are only about three million below the tax, and signing him to this would put them.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Shaedon Sharpe's injury and recovery timeline
quotes.excerpt: The Trail Blazers just officially announced that Shaedon Sharpe tore his meniscus last week in a workout.
quotes.quote: The Trail Blazers just officially announced that Shaedon Sharpe tore his meniscus last week in a workout and had surgery this week, and he will be re-evaluated in six months. Re-evaluated. So maybe not season-ending, but major season-impacting him.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Lack of rookie contract extensions across the NBA
quotes.excerpt: We've only had one of the rookies, rookie extensions get done, and that's Victor Wembanyama.
quotes.quote: We've only had one of the rookies, rookie extensions get done, and that's Victor Wembanyama. I was just talking to an executive yesterday about that. I was like, what have you heard on rookie extensions? And I was like, when I say rookie, I mean guys on their rookie contracts. I have heard nothing.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Jalen Duren's contract situation with the Pistons
quotes.excerpt: The one restricted free agency situation that remains unresolved is Jalen Duren.
quotes.quote: The one restricted free agency situation that remains unresolved is Jalen Duren, who the Pistons absolutely positively 100% intend to keep, and made it clear to anybody pursuing him in a sign and trade possibilities like, you're wasting your time.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Peyton Watson's potential breakout season with the Cleveland Cavaliers
quotes.excerpt: I think he's poised for a breakout. I think it's a great move for Cleveland.
quotes.quote: As I was talking to executives this week on doing our awards thing, I just had this guy throw in there. I didn't even ask about. He was like, by the way, I love this Peyton Watson move. I think he's poised for a breakout. I think it's a great move for Cleveland.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Mixed reviews on the Peyton Watson move for Cleveland
quotes.excerpt: I've heard mixed reviews on it.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: I've heard mixed reviews on it.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Yeah. This is the thing, these people that we're talking to, these are all lifetime, these guys have all been in the league, not all of them, but a lot of them, 20 plus years and have seen so much and evaluated so many players. It's fascinating when you will talk about the same topic to two different people and two people are like, a lot of times they're sort of in the middle.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Criticism of the Cavaliers' contract extension for Peyton Watson
quotes.excerpt: I cannot believe the Cavs gave Watson 90 million dollars based on one month.
quotes.quote: One guy going, oh man, I cannot believe the Cavs gave Watson 90 million dollars based on one month. And then I got this other guy who does player personnel, his job for his team is to do pro personnel, and by the way, I would say his team has done pretty well in pro personnel, margin moves in the last couple years. I would just say is, I respect him. And he's like, I love it. I love it.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's partnership with the PGA Tour in Akron
quotes.excerpt: LeBron and the PGA Tour made an agreement and announcement this week.
quotes.quote: LeBron and the PGA Tour made an agreement and announcement this week. First off, it's still jaw dropping to me that LeBron is this into golf. Talk about something I would never believe 15 years ago. A, that LeBron would still be playing and B, that he would be like crazy into golf.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The ongoing impact of LeBron James's I Promise School
quotes.excerpt: It's still impacting so many kids every single day.
quotes.quote: Because his I Promise School is now is not brand new, it's easy to forget. It's still impacting so many kids every single day. I remember back in 2015, going to Cedar Point, which is a famous amusement park in Ohio, and LeBron made this announcement to like a thousand of his kids that he brought there and paid for them to go in and everything for the day. And he's like, I'm giving you all college scholarships. I made a deal with the University of Akron and you guys are all going to get to go to college four years for free.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James's charitable impact on Akron education
quotes.excerpt: He has dramatically done things to impact the people of his community.
quotes.quote: He ended up doing the deal with Kent State University and the University of Akron. And I don't know, I'm sure the foundation could provide with me in 90 seconds how many kids took up on that. But that was 11 years ago. And some of those kids went to college for free because of it. My point is like, he has dramatically done things to impact the people of his community.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: The decline of the Firestone Country Club PGA event
quotes.excerpt: Firestone Country Club is a country club. I mean, what am I going to talk about a country club?
quotes.quote: Firestone Country Club is a country club. I mean, what am I going to talk about a country club? But this course, for decades, since dating back to like the 50s, had a PGA or senior PGA event every year. And it was a cornerstone. And unfortunately, LeBron's hometown and my hometown has been in basically a large decay over the last 30, 50 years or whatever. And it went from the PGA event down to a senior event and then it was sort of withering and people weren't supporting it and it lost its sponsors.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst

quotes.excerpt: How many times you played there?

text_blocks.text: How many times you played there?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I probably three times. LeBron has probably played there more this week than I've ever played there. He's a member.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: LeBron James partners with the PGA Tour for a new tournament
quotes.excerpt: LeBron, he made a deal with the PGA Tour. They're partnering.
quotes.quote: LeBron, he made a deal with the PGA Tour. They're partnering and starting next year, they're going to have a tournament there, which is sort of a minor league tournament that's part of the PGA Tour. And look, it's not going to be Tiger playing there.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Speculation on LeBron James playing in the new PGA tournament
quotes.excerpt: If they get LeBron, Steph, and you, the three biggest names ever born in Akron, this thing could be huge.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: Is LeBron going to play in it?

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Maybe by then, maybe he'll be trying to.

text_blocks.speaker: Tim Bontemps
text_blocks.text: I mean, if you want to get attention, if he plays in it, I promise you there will be TV cameras.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: I promise you, right. The point is that Firestone lost its tournament and LeBron makes, does something with the PGA Tour and brings something right back to Firestone that a bunch of people can be a part of and can be a part of his foundation.

quotes.quote: When they had the bubble, the only people playing golf, there was like three players, all the referees and coaches. There was no players. Yes, Steph Curry, you know, played a lot. But now all these guys playing golf.
